scripts.//dev: Starts everything: Postgres, the three .NET backends, the three frontends. The DB must be READY before the backends run — they migrate and seed on startup — so db:up and db:wait are sequential, and only then does the rest run in parallel.
scripts.dev: pnpm db:up && pnpm db:wait && concurrently -k -n em-api,dtd-api,host-api,em,dtd,host -c red,yellow,blue,magenta,green,cyan "pnpm:dev:em-api" "pnpm:dev:dtd-api" "pnpm:dev:host-api" "pnpm:dev:em" "pnpm:dev:dtd" "pnpm:dev:host"
scripts.//dev:apis: Each backend gets its own database, and its own port — the port lives in that project's Properties/launchSettings.json (host 5081, em 5082, dtd 5083), because a launch profile's applicationUrl overrides ASPNETCORE_URLS and setting it here would silently do nothing. sslmode=disable is required for LOCAL Postgres; Neon needs sslmode=require, which its own connection string already carries.
scripts.//db: Local Postgres only — production is Neon. db:reset DELETES the volume, so the next boot re-runs migrations and re-seeds from scratch. Calls go through scripts/container-cli.sh because `docker` is frequently a shell alias for podman, and aliases do not exist in the non-interactive shell that runs these scripts.
scripts.db:reset: bash scripts/container-cli.sh compose down -v && pnpm db:up && pnpm db:wait
scripts.db:psql: bash scripts/container-cli.sh compose exec postgres psql -U postgres
scripts.//deploy: There is no deploy script — Render builds and deploys every service from render.yaml on push. See the README.
